summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for June 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

eli5.summary: It is like a monthly count of how many cars used each road, written down so people can see which roads are busy.

questions: how much traffic did the arpanet carry in june 1973
how many packets did the arpanet carry in june 1973
which arpanet host sent the most packets in june 1973
subtitle: BBN's table of how many packets each ARPANET host sent in June 1973.

tldr.problem: ARPANET sites wanted to know how much traffic each host was generating.
tldr.mechanism: BBN-NET attached a Host Throughput Summary for June 1973, listing packets output per host, split into internode and intranode traffic.
tldr.outcome: The report gives monthly totals, daily averages and a ratio of packets to messages. RFC 556 later updated it.

today: RFC 538 is a one-month data report, and RFC 556 updates it. It has no protocol content to be current or outdated.

sections.title: What the Report Is
sections.content:
RFC 538, from A. McKenzie of BBN-NET and dated 5 July 1973, is a very short cover note: "Attached are the Host traffic statistics for the month of June 1973." The header says it updates RFC 522, the previous report.

Everything else is the attached table, titled HOST THROUGHPUT SUMMARY (PACKETS OUTPUT).
sections.eli5: A person at BBN sent around a monthly scoreboard of network traffic.

sections.title: How to Read the Table
sections.content:
Each row is a host at a site such as UCLA, SRI or MIT. For each host the table gives internode packets (sent between nodes), intranode packets (within the same node) and a total. Sites with several hosts also get a subtotal, the average daily internode packets, and the number of days counted (30 for most of June).

Some sites are listed as having had no traffic: BELV, ABER and LBL. NORSR was counted for 4 days.
sections.eli5: Each line says how many messages a computer sent to other places and how many it sent to its neighbors in the same room.

sections.title: Network Totals
sections.content:
The bottom of the table gives network-wide totals: 70245490 internode packets and 28609780 intranode packets. The daily averages are 2341516 internode and 953659 intranode, and the average per node-day is 64802 and 26393.

The last line gives PACKETS/MESSAGES (INTERNODE) as 1.07. Among the listed hosts, ISI HOST 1 had the most internode packets, 10795800.
sections.eli5: At the bottom, everything is added up, so you can see the whole network's busy-ness for the month.

references.text: RFC 522, the earlier traffic statistics report that this RFC's header says it updates.
